summary: AIHEC urges continued E‑Rate support for Tribal Colleges and Universities to honor federal trust obligations and advance education, workforce, and economic development in remote Indian communities. AIHEC argues that expanding E‑Rate eligibility to allow campus‑wide support for Tribal Colleges and Universities (TCUs) would increase participation and benefit TCUs and their students. The comment argues that Tribal College and University (TCU) libraries that serve as public libraries should be eligible for E‑Rate support, citing their role in rural communities and lack of alternative providers. The comment argues that tribal community university (TCU) libraries should be exempt from the regulation, citing their dual role, limited resources, and the fact that their operating costs are covered by Title III funding. Tribal colleges and universities (TCUs) argue for more flexible E‑Rate rules, including extended application windows, simplified cost‑allocation procedures, and exemption from mandatory lowest‑cost vendor selection.
